dataset: FAPT-Guard Synthetic Temporal ATT&CK Sequence Dataset

splits.definition: Complete timestamp-ordered normalized technique sequence, independent of IDs, host names and absolute time
splits.limitation: Repeated prefixes and sequences within a partition remain correlated; sample counts are not independent trial counts.

random_seed_usage: No randomized operation in evaluation; inherited training-comparison seed

metrics.top_k_reason: Top-k is NOT MEASURED when fewer than k trained classes exist

uncertainty.formula: -sum(p_i * ln(p_i), p_i > 0) / ln(K); K = all trained active classes, including zero-probability classes
uncertainty.interpretation: Dispersion of the complete model distribution, not probability of error or out-of-distribution reliability

calibration.calibration_method: Top-label ECE, 10 equal-width confidence bins; multiclass Brier score
calibration.calibration_dataset: FAPT-Guard Synthetic Temporal ATT&CK Sequence Dataset
calibration.scope: Aggregate synthetic held-out outcomes; not incident-specific calibration or fitted probability correction
calibration.brier_definition: Mean sum over union of trained and outcome classes; unseen true class has probability zero and contributes 1

conformal.target_coverage_scope: Configured design target only, not a measured guarantee
conformal.reason: Validation outcomes were already used to select this model; they are not an independent conformal calibration set. The unchanged test partition has 6 distinct full technique sequences. Keeping duplicates together and reserving a test group leaves fewer than 9 calibration groups needed for a finite, non-vacuous 90% split-conformal quantile. Validation/test contain targets outside the trained class space; a closed-label prediction set would exclude those outcomes. New labelled calibration and test sequence groups, unused for model selection and drawn from a defensible common distribution, are required.
conformal.proposed_method: Split conformal with score 1 - p(true class), one maximum score per independent sequence group; ceil((n+1)*target) order statistic
